# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

The integrity maintenance feature for [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java) has been implemented and verified.

### Summary of Changes

1. **Configuration Property & Initialization (`default.integrity`)**:
   - Added support for `default.integrity`, defaulting to `ignore` (which performs no checks).
   - When set to `repair`, the store inspects `stored.rules` and the folder on disk during [`initialize`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L118) by reloading the current state from disk, even if the store folder was previously initialized.

2. **Entry Classification (`broken`, `resolved`, `shared`)**:
   - **Shared**: Entries pointing to the identical file name string (even if nonexistent) or locating the same underlying file (via hard links, symbolic links, or real paths, including outside the store directory) are classified as shared. Shared entries and unreferenced files are never modified or discarded during integrity repair.
   - **Broken**: Entries whose file name is not a valid path or does not point to a regular file directly within the store folder (including nonexistent files, directories, subdirectories, or parent directory paths). Broken entries are discarded from `stored.rules`.
   - **Resolved**: Non-broken entries pointing to files with no violations (empty or containing only line breaks `\n` / `\r\n`). Resolved entries are discarded from `stored.rules`, and their files are deleted. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link directly within the folder, both the symlink and the target file it points to are deleted.

3. **Rule Forgetting on Save with `repair`**:
   - When saving an empty violations list (`violations.isEmpty()`) with `default.integrity=repair`:
     - **Unknown rule**: Nothing is saved (no file created, no index entry added).
     - **Known rule**: The rule is forgotten by removing its entry from `stored.rules` and deleting its file (and symlink target if applicable), unless another entry shares the file—in which case only the entry is removed.
     - **Deletion failure**: If deleting the file fails (e.g. `IOException`, permissions, non-empty directory), a [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) is thrown and the entry is left intact in `stored.rules`.

4. **Tests Added**:
   - Added comprehensive tests in [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java) covering `ignore` default behavior, broken entry removal, resolved entry and file cleanup (including symlinks), shared file handling (hardlinks, symlinks, same filenames, outside files), unreferenced file retention, disk re-check on repeated initialization, rule forgetting during `save`, and failure to delete leaving entries intact.
